Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients with signs or symptoms of heart disease.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient has a documented history of recurrent severe myocardial infarctions, coronary artery disease, ischemic cardiomyopathy, and impaired left ventricular function, all of which are clear signs of heart disease.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients selected because of either medical or research interest to the Principal Investigator.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: There is no explicit information in the patient profile indicating whether the Principal Investigator has selected this patient for medical or research interest.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients must not have unstable angina pectoris, unstable course following recent (within one month) myocardial infarction.
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient has a history of recurrent myocardial infarctions beginning at age 55, but the timing of the most recent myocardial infarction is not specified. It is unclear whether this occurred within the past month.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Must not be in New York Heart Association functional class IV heart failure.
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient has impaired left ventricular function and Stage III coronary artery disease, but the New York Heart Association functional class is not explicitly stated in the patient profile.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: A positive pregnancy test will obviate any cardiovascular testing requiring ionizing radiation.
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient is male, and pregnancy is not applicable to this individual.

Recap: The patient meets the inclusion criterion of having heart disease but lacks data on the Principal Investigator's interest. Exclusion criteria related to recent myocardial infarction and NYHA class IV heart failure are unclear due to missing information.
